newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire's ailing President Mobutu arrives in France.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's ailing President Mobutu arrives in France.

text.p: Zaire's ailing president Mobutu Sese Seko landed in his private plane at the French Riviera capital of Nice from Switzerland on Monday, an airport spokesman said.
The 66-year-old Zairean president, who has a villa near Nice, had been in Switzerland since August when he underwent surgery for prostate cancer at the University Hospital in Lausanne.
Mobutu arrived aboard a four-engined DC-8 aircraft specially designed for him and which can carry several dozen people, the spokesman said.

He made no statement on arrival and was whisked off to an undisclosed location presumed to be his sprawling personal residence at Roquebrune Cap-Martin, one of the choicest, most picturesque areas of the Riviera, just east of Monaco.

Officials in Paris said they did not know Mobutu was arriving and doubted he would meet President Jacques Chirac who is attending a Franco-Spanish summit in Marseille. That city is however relatively close to Nice.

Mobutu's arrival coincided with east Zaire falling into ever greater confusion. Fighting between rival groups has forced about a million refugees onto the roads and France has called for international action to help save them from disaster.

Mobutu, a one-time army sergeant who seized power in 1965, had been living with his entourage of more than 20 at Lausanne's luxury Beau-Rivage Palace hotel, but Swiss authorities were understood to have asked him to avoid public appearances or interviews.

A special United Nations envoy, Raymond Chretien, had been expecting to visit him in Lausanne this week to discuss fighting in eastern Zaire and the plight of a million Hutu refugees from Rwanda and Burundi.
Swiss television reported last month that Mobutu's villa in the south of France was being prepared for use and he might continue his treatment there.
Last week former French internal affairs minister Charles Pasqua visited him in Lausanne.
Mobutu's arrival in France places him in the country which is emerging as champion of foreign intervention in Zaire.

French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette had earlier in the day urged the United States, European and African countries on Monday to hold urgent talks on how to restore security in eastern Zaire and help avert disaster for more than one million refugees fleeing fighting.
